messages:
sam: Quick heads-up — spotted plaintext user emails and sessionId values in staging access logs for POST /api/v1/respond. Example below. Can we confirm redaction requirements so I can push a hotfix?

kevin: Can you paste the exact log snippet?

sam: Sure — snippet from staging (sanitized where I changed real domains):
```
[2026-03-17T09:20:11Z] POST /api/v1/respond 200 123ms 
headers={Authorization: Bearer sk_live_abc123, x-request-id: r-987, Content-Type: application/json} 
body={"user_email":"alice@example.com","sessionId":"s-5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99","prompt":"Hi my email is alice@example.com, please summarize my account"}
```

anjali: Do not persist Authorization tokens or raw prompts with PII. We should redact Authorization header entirely (e.g., Authorization: <REDACTED_TOKEN>), mask emails to <REDACTED_EMAIL>, and hash sessionId values before logging. For prompts, strip or redact PII (emails/phones/SSNs) or hash those fields.

miguel: Where is this logging happening? Ingress proxy or backend worker?

sam: Looks like the ingress proxy — we had debug body-logging enabled via a lua middleware in nginx for a short-lived debug build. That middleware writes full request body to our access logger.

kevin: Proposal: disable body logging in staging immediately and submit a PR to add a scrubber to the proxy. If we need to re-enable for repro, do it behind IP allowlist + 1-hour TTL. Need security approval for temporary enable.

security-bot: Reminder: company logging policy requires redaction of tokens and PII before persistence. See https://redwood.internal/security/logging-policy for details. Token values (Authorization, x-api-key) must never be stored in plaintext.

anjali: +1 to disabling body logging now. Kevin — open a small PR that: (1) removes debug body logging flag, (2) adds a middleware scrub step with email regex -> <REDACTED_EMAIL>, token header -> <REDACTED_TOKEN>, and sessionId -> sha256(sessionId) in logs. Add unit tests. If you need to temporarily enable debug, limit to IPs + TTL 1 hour and tag @eng-security.

miguel: For permanent fix, let's update our logging-lib so all services share scrub rules. Rules: email -> <REDACTED_EMAIL>, credit-card -> <REDACTED_CC>, token-like patterns -> <REDACTED_TOKEN>, sessionId -> hash. Add integration test that scans logs for unsubstituted email regex.

kevin: I'll open PR and a Jira (SECLOG-321) for tracking. Who can approve a one-time flip for repro?

sam: Can @anjali or @miguel approve? We want to repro a client-side flow that only appears with body logging on.

anjali: I approve a one-time flip for 30 minutes starting on request, only from your workstation IP and sysadmin IPs. Must purge any generated logs afterwards (S3 lifecycle or delete) and document in the Jira. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: staging-config-rollout by kevin at 1763501500.

kevin: Deploying now — removed debug flag and added a temporary scrubber (matches email regex) in nginx. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/4123. I'll link Jira SECLOG-321.

anjali: Thanks. I reviewed the PR quickly — unit tests look good. Please ensure the scrubber does not alter base64 blobs and only targets text fields.

kevin: Confirmed. Also added a regex whitelist to avoid touching model payloads.

security-bot: Note: if any logs containing PII were ingested to long-term storage, escalate to sec-ops. We require purging and an audit log entry for the purge.

sam: Ran a grep across staging logs at 1763501899 — no email patterns found in the last 24h after the change. Will keep monitoring for 48h.

kevin: PR merged and config rolled out. Closing the temporary debug window.

anjali: Marking this as resolved on our side — follow up in SECLOG-321 to move scrub rules into shared logging-lib and add backward scans to catch older leaks.

security-bot: Thread marked resolved (pending Jira verification).

sam: Thanks everyone :thumbsup: Verified and closing thread.
